summary: Full E2E test of Erchis Fantasy Dice RPG Phase 1 MVP. Backend: 31/32 pytest tests pass (1 failure is a test-expectation mismatch, not a bug — server checks 'already learned' before teacher existence). Frontend: complete flow verified — landing → register → 5-step character wizard → game HUD → tutorial → gather (dice+narrative) → hunt (combat screen → victory + drops) → all tabs (inv/forge/skills/map) → leaderboard → logout → re-login persistence. All 14 features in the request list are functional.

minor.issue: When a character already knows the skill AND the teacher is invalid, server returns 409 'Skill already learned' (checked before teacher lookup). Test expectation harmless; consider validating teacher first for clearer errors.

Status effects are appended to character.statuses without deduplication/merging — same status (e.g. BLEEDING) stacks into 7+ instances after repeated action fails. Consider merging duration/magnitude or capping.

ui_bugs.issue: Tutorial overlay re-appears on every login/reload even for existing characters that have completed/skipped the tutorial. tutorial_complete flag on the character doesn't appear to suppress it. Not critical but adds friction.
Multiple identical BLEEDING statuses render as separate pill chips (7 chips of BLEEDING shown). Visual clutter caused by backend not deduping statuses.

issues: Design intentionally uses hard borders + VT323 pixel font — as noted in task, not reported as a bug. Amber/dark palette + rarity color-borders on inventory tiles render correctly (common=gray, uncommon=green, rare=blue, epic=purple).

action_items: OPTIONAL: Merge/dedupe status effects instead of appending duplicates (server.py do_action + combat).
OPTIONAL: Ensure tutorial overlay respects character.tutorial_complete flag on subsequent sessions.
OPTIONAL: In /api/game/skill/learn, validate teacher_id before the 'already learned' check for clearer 404 responses.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 750+ lines — reasonable for MVP but consider splitting auth, character, action, combat, craft, skills, daily into /routes modules (dir already exists but empty).
resolve_action + combat_turn append status pills without dedup — see minor issues above.
GET /game/character silently mutates DB (touches login streak/dailies) — semantically GET should be idempotent; safe for this MVP but noteworthy.
CORS: allow_origins=['*'] in backend .env is unused; server.py hardcodes FRONTEND_URL origin — good, cookies (SameSite=None; Secure) correctly configured for cross-domain.
MongoDB ObjectId correctly stripped via _serialize_doc; world_events response also strips _id.
data-testid coverage is excellent across all components — testing was frictionless.
test_credentials: test@erchis.io / password123 (Erethon L1 Human/Fighter/Knight) — confirmed working. Fresh registrations via UI + API also working.
seed_data_creation: Two test users created during testing: TESTHero (fresh reg via API for character-creation test), TestBladeUI (fresh reg via Playwright UI flow — Human/Fighter/Knight w/ oath). Left in DB for regression.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All feature flows in the phase-1 spec are functional. If retest needed, focus on: (1) tutorial persistence across sessions, (2) status-effect dedup, (3) daily mission claim happy path (requires actually completing a mission — 3 wolf kills or 5 herb gathers via repeated /api/game/action calls with dice luck). The /leaderboard route works but is a separate page (not tab); the 'tab-leaderboard' element is a link that navigates via react-router. Combat auto-selects skills/items but manual override buttons (skill-manual-*, item-manual-*) also render and work.
rca of the issue: Only one test failed (TestSkills.test_learn_skill_invalid_teacher expected 404 for a bogus teacher, got 409). Root cause: server.py at line 607 checks `any(s.get('skill_id') == skill_id ...)` BEFORE looking up teacher, so if the character already learned the skill the server correctly returns 409 without validating the teacher. Erethon starts with 'shield_bash' as a Knight, so the request short-circuited to 409. This is a test-side expectation error, not a bug — behavior is defensible.
